name: Agricultural Records & Bookkeeping

objectives.text: Describe why farmers and ranchers keep records of what they buy, sell, and grow
Record daily production data such as eggs collected, feed fed, or plant growth in a simple log
Explain the difference between income and expenses in a farm record book
Calculate the profit or loss of a small agricultural project by subtracting total expenses from total income
Identify the main sections of an SAE record book, including inventory, income, expenses, and hours worked
Record SAE transactions in a journal with the date, description, and amount, using receipts and sales slips as source documents
Classify farm transactions as assets, liabilities, income, or expenses
Distinguish between current and noncurrent assets and between capital and noncapital items when building a beginning inventory
Apply double-entry principles by recording agricultural business transactions as debits and credits to the correct accounts
Compare cash and accrual accounting methods and explain how each records income and expenses for a farm business
Maintain SAE records in the Agricultural Experience Tracker, including beginning and ending inventories, capital purchases, income, expenses, and hours
Reconcile a farm checking account register with a bank statement to locate and correct recording errors
Compare the purposes of balance sheets, income statements, cash flow statements, and statements of owner equity and how often each is used to monitor an agricultural business
Interpret a balance sheet and an income statement to assess the net worth and profitability of an agricultural business
Calculate straight-line depreciation for machinery, buildings, or purchased breeding livestock and record it on a depreciation schedule
Prepare inventory reports that calculate cost of goods sold and gross margin for an agricultural production or retail enterprise
Calculate and interpret financial ratios such as the current ratio, debt-to-asset ratio, and rate of return on assets for a farm or ranch
Analyze a cash flow statement to identify periods of surplus and shortfall in an agricultural operation
Develop a cash budget for an SAE enterprise that projects anticipated revenue, production costs, and overhead costs
Calculate cost of production per unit and break-even price and yield from enterprise records
Analyze how recording the purchase of a major capital asset such as a tractor changes the balance sheet, depreciation schedule, and cash flow of an agricultural business
Prepare verified SAE financial summaries of earnings, productive investment, and hours for an FFA degree or proficiency award application
Evaluate enterprise records to recommend whether to expand, adjust, or discontinue an agricultural enterprise
Manage a complete set of agricultural financial records and prepare an accurate balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement

changes: Kept all six existing objectives, rewording the grade 10 item to name net worth and profitability, and anchored the high school ones to AFNR codes. Added missing competencies across the span: production logs, project profit or loss, SAE record book sections and journaling, capital versus noncapital and current versus noncurrent items, debits and credits, cash versus accrual, AET record keeping, bank reconciliation, comparing financial report types, depreciation schedules, inventory and cost of goods sold, financial ratios, SAE cash budgets, cost of production and break-even, capital asset effects, FFA degree and proficiency summaries, and enterprise evaluation. Tax reporting, credit, risk, and business organization standards were left to the sibling sub-topics.
